chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The estate of the missing person (mafqud) is withheld for the heirs for as long as he is sought in the land for four years; if he is not found, his estate is distributed among the heirs. And if he has a child, his estate is withheld and spent on his child for those four years.

key_terms.الْمَفْقُودُ: The missing person (one whose whereabouts are unknown)
key_terms.يُحْبَسُ: Is withheld / detained (estate is not distributed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the inheritance of a missing person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the standard four-year period for a missing person (mafqud) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between general heirs and descendants. It highlights the juristic priority of preserving the child's maintenance (nafaqah) from the estate during the search period, reflecting the principle of protecting vulnerable dependents before final distribution. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for later scholars when debating the exact duration and conditions of inheritance distribution for the missing.
